newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Deal to end strike at Cambior Omai mine.
newsitem.headline: Deal to end strike at Cambior Omai mine.

text.p: An agreement was reached Thursday to end a two-day strike at Cambior's Omai Gold Mines in Guyana, the company said.
It said in a press release that "all employees who took strike action with effect from Tuesday, August 12 will return to work at 6.00 p.m. (local) today, August 14."
The agreement between Omai Gold Mines management and the Guyana Bauxite and General Workers Union stipulated there would be "no victimization or intimidation of those workers who were on strike."
The work stoppage did not affect output and the mill remained in operation, a company spokeswoman said earlier by telephone from the Guyanese capital of Georgetown.
She said over 200 workers were on strike, out of a total workforce of more than 900, in protest over disciplinary measures applied to two employees.
The press release said the measures, a suspension and a dismissal, would be reviewed by management and union delegates.
Montreal-based Cambior Inc owns 65 percent of the open-pit mine, U.S. Golden Star Resources Ltd 30 percent and the Guyanese government the rest.
Cambior has projected gold production at Omai to increase to 340,000 ounces this year, from 255,000 ounces in 1996.
Gold is Guyana's second foreign currency earner after sugar if one includes Omai gold mine, the largest foreign investment in the country.
